[quote=the_crystalline_empire;60530446]At this point Rochambeau interjected, rising to his feet and addressing the king, Your majesty, it is clear that this man means to lecture you and our nation on how it ought to be run, he has come here disguised as a dealer of funds and of cooperation, but now, he reveals himself a snake!

The king looked at Rochambeau with moderation and replied, Cardinal Rochambeau, who is in charge here? Was it not I that permitted these to come and see me? 

Nay, it wasnt even you, but the ministers, stated Villiard, And in the powers of the president of the state, the duchess! He replied, leaping to his feet.

Gentlemen, intoned the duchess once more, Listen to what comrade Lo Pilato is warning of, if we should wish to preserve ourselves, we must consider the realities, or do you not know that the workers are still yet disgruntled in their unions, she continued.

However the king waved his hand dismissive of her and turned once again to his guests, What? Would you have us live in hovels and kruschevkas to sustain the order of the masses? Would you have us destroy tradition and faith and become a muddling farce, like the neo-imperialist state of Thýven? Their ministers kowtow in the streets to the poor and hold two residences, one of finery, and another in the poorest regions of their state, as if that promotes equality and isnt simply performative piety, [/quote]
"People criticize the cause of communism as being deterministic, that the very foundation of the communist dialectic is the assumed fury of an oppressed people against a system that exploits it, and that through this presumption all of communism waits for a violence that may not come. However, I believe that this determinism is what perfects communism. Coldness does not exist. We created that word to understand the absence of heat. In the same way there is no active and emanating evil; there is only the absence of good. The capitalist system does not manufacture evil, it is simply proceeds itself devoid of the goodness that is inherent in this human race that will soon rout it all out."

Lo Pilato continued, refusing to back down from his position. Normally, Sanguinian delegations would not be this forceful, but Lo Pilato was one of the great theoreticians of the Socialist International. To him, the compliance of the Montfleurois was the first necessary step in order for Elseyro-communism to flourish for ever. He thus concluded.

"If you believe God, then you should believe that good will triumph over evil, that one day this meaningless ruin will end and the life we have lived will be recompensed with eternity. Just because capitalism has created skyscrapers and beautiful skyscrapers does not mean that communism is incapable of doing the same. What we envision is, at the end of this day, happiness, for every man, until the return of the greatest Creator."

Before he could wait for either the King to voice his reservations, the Cardinal his complaints and accusations, or Villiard's ecstastic approval, Lo Pilato then turned to his absent-minded minister, who at this point had been staying out of the conversation. "Comrade Terrasi,", he called out to her.

"Wuh?"

"Over here, please."

"It's for this reason that I've brought along Comrade Terrasi here." Lo Pilato continued, beckoning for Terrasi to step in between himself and the Montfleurois. "She has now informed you all of what must be done in order to enrich our nations, in accordance with the capitalist system that we must operate in on the long journey to communism. Her ideas are comprehensive, realistic, and attuned to the way of life that the Montfleuroisie are familiar with. We may settle with her vision as the minimum program, but I wish that Your Majesty and your honorable government consider the maximum program too, for our shared defense against the people's enemy. Right, comrade?"

"Oh, er... yes, well, to be honest I don't really think I'm all that cut out for geopolitical cases..." Terrasi meekly replied, adjusting her sunglasses. "But hey, if my ideas could be a stepping stone to a future in which Sanguivallis and Montfleur could be together under a single fraternal union, then that would be pretty good. Um, Your Majesty."

The duchess having heard it all spoke following this, holding her hand out to stimy any objections from the other men of the room, I give assent to your arguments, and to your ideas, it is good to consider the ploy of the people, and to walk not in pietistic order, but in true order. Now it is known in every society that there is a particular order to which that society is bound to, wherein it takes an act of tremendous universal assent to turn that order, for order twisted by one group or one person is not true order, but manufactured. Communism devolves ultimately into the restoration of the prior order of tyranny, or is not Qianxun an example? Sanguivallis may be free now, but who holds the councils and the government accountable, is not even the presence of government an act of placing individuals higher than that of the rest? Or what man will respect the leader who sits beneath him or beside him? Unless society removes itself of its differences and of the individuality of the human person, true equality cannot be achieved. However, each man is called to live according to his calling, and we are commanded to respect those in authority. Yet Communism, under its ideal, tears down the authority in an attempt to solve oppression, and in its stead it causes more oppression as anything against communism is seen as evil, whether it be king or president, or the man who has the extra penny. She paused before continuing.

It is thus that the chances of Montfleur flipping a dime and making the maximum shift towards the ideals of communism are far less than that of Thýven, or the EDU marching into our borders to supress our very own liberality, however, the opines of comrade Terassi are well recieved and well wanted, as such, I say yes to your offer, and I have the authority to approve of such!
